source_meta._title: Skulls, signs, hanging signs, banners and decorated pots have no breaking/sprinting particles

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4 in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world, using the unmodified vanilla client. Cheats are enabled for switching to Survival mode. The particle setting is set to All. The reproduction target is a top-placed Skeleton Skull, which is available in the first listed affected version.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Java Edition 1.14.4; do not use the fix version 24w46a.
Use an unmodified vanilla client without mods, shaders, or resource packs that alter block or particle rendering.
Use default controls unless rebound: E opens the inventory, T opens chat, right-click uses or places a block, and left-click performs the Attack/Destroy action.
The executor must be able to see the game view clearly enough to monitor the area immediately around the target block during a short punching action.
Use a disposable test world so that changing game mode and placing test blocks cannot affect an important world.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for Java Edition 1.14.4 and start the game. Do not select 24w46a or another fix version.
steps.success_cue: The title screen displays Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer and then Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and cycle World Type until Superflat is selected. Confirm the options and create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode Superflat world opens, with a level grass surface visible around the player.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until the nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement and camera controls respond without loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The nearby Superflat terrain is rendered, and the player can move and turn normally.

steps.action: Open the pause menu and navigate to Options, then Video Settings. Find the Particles setting and cycle it until it reads All. Return to the game.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options... -> Video Settings... -> Particles: All -> Done -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed and the Video Settings menu was left with Particles set to All.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Select the Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon, click the search field, and enter "stone". Locate the ordinary Stone block and place one stack into hotbar slot 1 by clicking or dragging it there.
steps.success_cue: Stone is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, replace the search text with "skeleton skull". Locate the item named Skeleton Skull and place one into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: A Skeleton Skull is present in hotbar slot 2, while Stone remains in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to the world.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and the hotbar contains Stone in slot 1 and a Skeleton Skull in slot 2.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1, point at a nearby grass block, and right-click its top face once to place one Stone block above the ground.
steps.success_cue: One full Stone block is standing directly above the grass surface.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2. Aim at the top face of the newly placed Stone block and right-click once to place the Skeleton Skull on top of it.
steps.success_cue: A Skeleton Skull is visibly placed on the top face of the Stone block rather than on its side.

steps.action: Stand on the grass next to the test block and adjust the camera so the placed Skeleton Skull is clearly visible and can be reached without moving. Do not stand directly on the skull.
steps.success_cue: The skull is within normal interaction range and remains fully visible in the game view.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat input. The command must be run in the client chat, not in an external console.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the game-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command completes, and opening the inventory would now show the Survival inventory and crafting layout instead of the Creative item-selection interface.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is using an empty hand. Because only slots 1 and 2 were used during setup, select slot 3 unless another item is already there.
steps.success_cue: No held item is visible in the player's hand, while the Stone and Skeleton Skull remain in other hotbar slots.

steps.action: Center the crosshair directly on the placed Skeleton Skull. Confirm that the outline or targeting response corresponds to the skull and not the supporting Stone block.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is held steadily on the Skeleton Skull, the skull is within reach, and the supporting Stone block is not the intended target.

steps.action: With the crosshair kept on the Skeleton Skull, press and hold the Attack/Destroy control, which is the left mouse button by default, for approximately 0.5 seconds. Release the button before the skull is completely broken. Perform only this one short partial-breaking attempt, and do not continue until the block disappears.
steps.exact_input: Left Mouse Button (hold for approximately 0.5 seconds, then release before the skull breaks)
steps.success_cue: One short Survival-mode punching/partial-breaking action has been applied directly to the skull, and the Skeleton Skull remains placed on the Stone block.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just completed one short empty-hand Survival-mode punch against the targeted Skeleton Skull, the attack was released before the skull broke, and the skull remains placed and visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the visual output recorded during that partial-breaking action.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section. This minimum path is reconstructed from the description stating that punching affected blocks is a trigger.

The first affected version, 1.14.4, predates hanging signs and decorated pots. To comply with affected-version selection requirements, this plan uses a Skeleton Skull, which is explicitly identified as affected and exists in 1.14.4.

The issue covers several block families, but a Skeleton Skull was selected as the simplest deterministic representative target. Signs and banners can be substituted in separate breaking-particle variants, but those variants are not required by this single execution path.

A report comment states that banner and sign sprinting-particle variants are impossible to test in unmodified vanilla 1.14.4 because those blocks have no collision box. This plan therefore uses the punching/partial-breaking trigger rather than attempting those sprinting variants.
The exact safe hold duration before the skull breaks can vary slightly with input timing. The executor must prioritize releasing the Attack/Destroy control while the skull is still present.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-13842:When you ride a horse tied to a block the rope breaks, but the rope on the block doesn't | Cloners:inward:MC-239902:Weather effects appear in caves and structures in 1.17.1 worlds loaded in 21w43a | Duplicate:inward:MCL-13842:Maps show stone pattern despite it not being there and rain under solid blocks | Duplicate:inward:MCL-13881:Rain/weather
source_meta._title: Rain falls through any blocks in some spots

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition dedicated server reproduction. Create and save the test world using a matching 1.15.2 server/client first, and then open that same unoptimized world using a matching 20w17a server/client. Use one operator test player in a normal Overworld. Do not use --forceUpgrade, --eraseCache, Optimize World, Erase cached data, or any third-party server software, mods, shaders, or optimization tools.
preconditions: Have separate, working vanilla Minecraft Java Edition server executables for 1.15.2 and snapshot 20w17a.
Have matching vanilla client installations for 1.15.2 and 20w17a. Snapshot versions must be enabled in the Minecraft Launcher to make 20w17a available.
Use a dedicated-server world folder that can be preserved unchanged when switching the server executable from 1.15.2 to 20w17a.
The test player's account name must be known so it can be granted operator permission for /gamemode, /fill, and /weather.

Use a normal Overworld and locate a rain-capable biome such as plains or forest; do not perform the test in a desert, savanna, badlands, or a cold biome where visible precipitation is absent or becomes snow.
Back up the complete world folder after the 1.15.2 preparation phase and before opening it in 20w17a.

Do not optimize the world or erase its cached data before or during reproduction, because the report identifies cache erasure as a remediation procedure rather than part of the original triggering setup.

steps.action: Configure a clean vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 dedicated server to create a normal Overworld. Start the server and wait for initial world generation to finish.
steps.success_cue: The server console reports that startup is complete, normally with a message beginning with "Done", and the server is accepting connections.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, grant operator permission to the test player. Enter the command without a leading slash, replacing the placeholder with the exact Minecraft account name.
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the named player is now an operator.

steps.action: Launch vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 and connect the test player to the 1.15.2 dedicated server.
steps.success_cue: The player has joined the Overworld, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Switch the test player to Creative mode. Press T to open chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the player has the Creative-mode inventory and can fly by double-tapping Space.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug screen. Travel through the Overworld until the biome entry reports a rain-capable biome, preferably minecraft:plains or minecraft:forest. Choose a reasonably flat location with enough open space around it for a 64-by-64-block test roof.
steps.success_cue: The debug screen identifies the current biome as minecraft:plains or minecraft:forest, and the surrounding chunks have finished rendering.

steps.action: Stand at the intended center of the covered test area. Use the F3 debug screen to record the player's current X, Y, and Z coordinates so the same position can be recovered after the version change. Remain stationary after recording them.
steps.success_cue: The center X, Y, and Z coordinates have been recorded and the player is stationary at that position.

steps.action: Create a large solid stone roof in the old-version world. While still at the recorded center, press T, enter the exact /fill command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command creates a one-block-thick 64-by-64 roof eight blocks above the player and spans several chunks to provide many covered test positions.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, a continuous stone ceiling is visible overhead, and the server reports that the fill operation completed. No opening should be present directly above the player.

steps.action: Look upward and move only enough to confirm that the roof consists of solid stone and extends at least 32 blocks in each horizontal direction from the recorded center. Return to the recorded center coordinates and remain underneath the roof.
steps.success_cue: The player is back at the recorded center with the solid stone roof eight blocks overhead and with old-version chunks containing the roof loaded around the player.

steps.action: Cleanly stop the 1.15.2 dedicated server so that the generated chunks, placed roof blocks, weather data, and player position are written to disk. Enter the command in the server console without a leading slash.
steps.success_cue: All players are disconnected and the server process exits normally after saving the world.

steps.action: Make a complete backup copy of the stopped 1.15.2 world folder. Keep the original active world folder available for the version upgrade.
steps.success_cue: A separate backup exists, while the active server folder still contains the same level.dat, region data, player data, and other world files created by 1.15.2.

steps.action: Configure the dedicated server to run vanilla snapshot 20w17a while retaining the exact same active world folder and level-name. Do not generate a replacement world, and do not add --forceUpgrade or --eraseCache to the server startup command.
steps.success_cue: The 20w17a server is configured to load the world previously saved by 1.15.2, with no cache-erasure or forced-upgrade arguments enabled.

steps.action: Start the 20w17a dedicated server and allow it to open or convert the existing world. Do not interrupt the process.
steps.success_cue: The server reaches its normal startup-complete state and accepts connections using the same world rather than creating a new one.

steps.action: Launch vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 20w17a and connect the same test player to the 20w17a server.
steps.success_cue: The player joins the upgraded world and the previously created stone roof is present.

steps.action: Do not run any weather command immediately after joining. Wait until the roof and surrounding chunks have rendered completely and player movement, chat commands, and server responses are normal.
steps.success_cue: The player can move and use commands without chunk-loading pauses, and the old-version stone roof is fully rendered overhead.

steps.action: Confirm that the player is at the recorded center underneath the stone roof. If the saved login position differs, use the recorded X, Y, and Z values to return there before continuing. Keep the player's head below the roof and do not break or replace any roof blocks in 20w17a.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary at the old-version test area's recorded center, with an uninterrupted solid stone roof overhead.

steps.action: Establish a controlled clear-weather starting state. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The server accepts the command and confirms that the weather has been changed to clear while the player remains beneath the roof.

steps.action: Wait briefly without moving or editing the roof so the clear-weather state is applied and the server remains responsive.
steps.success_cue: The server is responsive, the player remains beneath the center of the unchanged roof, and no world-conversion or chunk-loading activity is still occurring.

steps.action: Trigger rainy weather while the player is stationary under the stone roof. Press T, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after the server accepts the command; do not optimize the world, replace roof blocks, or change dimensions.
steps.success_cue: The server accepts the rain command while the player remains beneath the center of the 1.15.2-created stone roof in the upgraded 20w17a world.

stor.handoff_condition: The 20w17a server has just accepted /weather rain while the player is stationary beneath the center of the unchanged 64-by-64 stone roof created and saved in 1.15.2. The same unoptimized world is loaded, surrounding chunks are fully rendered, and the server is responsive. The observation subsystem should now take control and inspect the covered area, including positions across the roof's multi-chunk footprint.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce, world seed, coordinates, downloadable world, or exact affected location. The plan reconstructs a minimal cross-version procedure from the description and comments.

The original description only says that the problem occurred on a snapshot server after an update; it does not identify the exact version that originally created the world. Version 1.15.2 is used for world creation because a moderator explicitly discussed testing worlds upgraded from 1.15.2, and comments describe the issue in worlds originating in previous versions.

The 64-by-64 stone roof is a practical test fixture rather than a structure specified by the reporter. It is intentionally created before upgrading so that several covered, previously saved chunks are available for inspection in 20w17a.

The report characterizes affected positions as random and provides no deterministic coordinates. Consequently, this prepared roof may not intersect an affected position in every newly generated world; reproducing may require another pre-20w17a world or another previously generated area, but the report does not provide evidence for selecting a specific alternative location.

The description mentions both a Y-level 30 cave and a house but does not provide enough spatial information to reconstruct either original location. The broad solid roof is used as the simplest supported covered-area substitute.
No external web verification was used; historical commands in this plan are operational additions and were not copied from the report.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-221864:Iron golems produce walking particles for light blocks | Relates:inward:MC-249384:Warden can create light, barrier and structure void particles when digging
source_meta._title: Inconsistency: Barriers and structure voids produce particles when broken, but light blocks do not

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 21w13a in a singleplayer world using the integrated server. The player must be in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled. Set the client particle option to All so the comparison is not affected by reduced particle settings. Use default controls or the equivalent rebound controls.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is configured to make historical Java Edition snapshots available, and snapshot 21w13a can be launched.
Use an unmodified client without mods or resource packs that alter block models, invisible-block rendering, or particles.
The test world must permit commands. The simplest setup is a new singleplayer Creative-mode world with Allow Cheats set to ON.
The player must have enough unobstructed space to place three separated pedestal blocks and one test block above each pedestal.
The observation system must be ready before the first test block is broken and must remain active until all three comparison blocks have been broken.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation whose version is exactly snapshot 21w13a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Launcher -> Installations -> New installation or Edit -> Version: snapshot 21w13a -> Play
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu and displays 21w13a as the running version.

steps.action: Create a new singleplayer world. Set Game Mode to Creative and set Allow Cheats to ON before creating it. No particular seed or world type is required; a flat, open spawn area is preferable but not mandatory.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The world loads with the player in Creative mode, indicated by the absence of health and hunger bars and the ability to fly by double-tapping Space.

steps.action: Wait for world loading to finish before preparing the test. Do not continue while nearby terrain is still appearing or player controls are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are rendered, the player can turn and move normally, and opening chat responds immediately.

steps.action: Configure the client to display all particles. Open the pause menu, enter the video settings, and cycle the Particles option until it reads All. Return to the world afterward.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> Particles: All -> Done -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen showed Particles: All, and the player has returned to the world.

steps.action: Obtain three ordinary stone blocks for use as visible pedestals. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Three Stone blocks are present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command does not produce a red syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Obtain one Barrier item. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A Barrier item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command does not produce a red syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Obtain one Structure Void item. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A Structure Void item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command does not produce a red syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Obtain one Light block item. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. No BlockStateTag is necessary for this break-particle comparison; the default light level is sufficient.
steps.success_cue: A Light item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command does not produce a red syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Open the inventory with E. Arrange Stone, Barrier, Structure Void, and Light into four separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the inventory and at the bottom of the normal game screen. Close the inventory with E when finished.
steps.exact_input: E; drag Stone, Barrier, Structure Void, and Light into separate hotbar slots; E
steps.success_cue: All four item types are visible in separate hotbar slots and can be selected individually with their corresponding number keys or the mouse wheel.

steps.action: Move to a clear patch of solid ground. Select Stone, then place three single Stone pedestal blocks in a straight horizontal row by right-clicking the ground. Leave one empty horizontal block between adjacent pedestals so the three test positions cannot overlap. Treat them as the left, middle, and right pedestals while facing the row.
steps.exact_input: Select the Stone hotbar slot; right-click the ground three times with one empty block between placements
steps.success_cue: Three separate Stone blocks form a clearly visible row with one-block gaps: a left pedestal, a middle pedestal, and a right pedestal.

steps.action: Select the Barrier item in the hotbar. Aim at the top face of the left Stone pedestal and right-click once to place a Barrier directly above it.
steps.exact_input: Select Barrier; aim at the top of the left pedestal; right-click once
steps.success_cue: While the Barrier item remains selected, the Barrier's visible marker appears in the one-block space directly above the left Stone pedestal.

steps.action: Select the Structure Void item. Aim at the top face of the middle Stone pedestal and right-click once to place a Structure Void directly above it.
steps.exact_input: Select Structure Void; aim at the top of the middle pedestal; right-click once
steps.success_cue: While the Structure Void item remains selected, its special marker appears in the one-block space directly above the middle Stone pedestal.

steps.action: Select the Light item. Aim at the top face of the right Stone pedestal and right-click once to place a Light block directly above it. Do not right-click the placed Light block again, because additional right-clicks cycle its light level and are unnecessary for this test.
steps.exact_input: Select Light; aim at the top of the right pedestal; right-click once
steps.success_cue: While the Light item remains selected, the Light block's marker appears in the one-block space directly above the right Stone pedestal.

steps.action: Move approximately two to four blocks away from the front of the pedestal row and face all three pedestals. Adjust the camera so each test position can be targeted without moving far between breaks.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls, normally W/A/S/D, and mouse look
steps.success_cue: The left, middle, and right pedestals are distinguishable and all three test positions are within easy camera reach.

steps.action: Select the Barrier item so the placed Barrier is visible and targetable. Center the crosshair on the Barrier marker directly above the left pedestal. Do not click until the observation system is ready.
steps.exact_input: Select Barrier; move the crosshair onto the marker above the left pedestal
steps.success_cue: The Barrier marker above the left pedestal is visible and outlined under the crosshair, ready to be broken.

steps.action: With the crosshair still on the Barrier above the left pedestal, left-click once to break it in Creative mode. This is the first trigger action; particle observation must begin no later than this click.
steps.success_cue: While the Barrier item is still selected, the Barrier marker is no longer present above the left Stone pedestal.

steps.action: Select the Structure Void item so the placed Structure Void can be identified. Center the crosshair on the Structure Void marker directly above the middle pedestal.
steps.exact_input: Select Structure Void; move the crosshair onto the marker above the middle pedestal
steps.success_cue: The Structure Void marker above the middle pedestal is visible and targeted by the crosshair.

steps.action: With the crosshair still on the Structure Void above the middle pedestal, left-click once to break it in Creative mode.
steps.success_cue: While the Structure Void item is still selected, the Structure Void marker is no longer present above the middle Stone pedestal.

steps.action: Select the Light item so the placed Light block becomes visible and targetable. Center the crosshair on the Light marker directly above the right pedestal.
steps.exact_input: Select Light; move the crosshair onto the marker above the right pedestal
steps.success_cue: The Light block marker above the right pedestal is visible and targeted by the crosshair.

steps.action: With the crosshair still on the Light block above the right pedestal, left-click once to break it in Creative mode.
steps.success_cue: While the Light item is still selected, the Light block marker is no longer present above the right Stone pedestal. Each of the three test blocks has now been broken exactly once in the order Barrier, Structure Void, Light.

stor.handoff_condition: Begin observation at step 16, when the Barrier is first broken, and keep observation active through steps 18 and 20. Handoff is complete after the Barrier, Structure Void, and Light block have each been broken exactly once in that order while Particles remains set to All; the three Stone pedestals remain in place and the spaces directly above them are empty.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section. The minimum deterministic path was reconstructed from the description's statement that a Creative-mode player breaks the three command-exclusive invisible blocks.

The description refers once to a 'structure block,' but the issue title, labels, and later wording specifically identify Structure Void. This plan therefore tests minecraft:structure_void rather than minecraft:structure_block.

The report also mentions punching, sprinting, falling, and iron-golem walking as other circumstances that can create particles. Those secondary variants are not included because breaking each block once is the primary and safest deterministic reproduction described by the issue.
The pedestal arrangement, particle-setting check, and Barrier -> Structure Void -> Light order are execution aids rather than report-mandated requirements.

External verification was used for the 21w13a Light block's command-only acquisition and held-item visibility/targetability behavior, and for the relevant Java Edition item identifiers and /give syntax.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-240028:Water and lava have dedicated minecraft:block particles
source_meta._title: Iron golems can produce particles for blocks they're not colliding with

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20 Pre-release 1 in a clean, unmodded single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server. Use default resources, enable cheats/commands, and set particle rendering to All. The deterministic coordinates and command-built arena below are a practical reconstruction because the report's five image attachments and part of the sentence describing where to create the golem are absent from the supplied report.
preconditions: Use exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20 Pre-release 1, the first and only version listed as affected. Do not use the fix version, 1.20 Pre-release 3, for reproduction.
Use a separate test installation and test world so an old pre-release does not open or modify an important world.
Use the vanilla client without mods, shaders, or resource packs that replace or suppress block particles.
Create the world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled. A Superflat world is preferred only to provide an unobstructed construction area; no seed is specified by the report.
Set particle rendering to All before spawning the iron golem.

The supplied report refers to an attached image for the precise setup, but the image content is unavailable. The specified runway, contrasting side blocks, and invisible containment walls are a practical reconstruction intended to keep the golem from colliding with the contrasting blocks while it walks near them.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Installations, enable access to snapshot/pre-release installations if necessary, create an installation using exactly Java Edition 1.20 Pre-release 1, and launch it. Keep this installation in a separate game directory if the launcher exposes that option.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and identifies the running version as 1.20 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new disposable world in Creative mode, enable Allow Cheats, and preferably select the Superflat world type. Enter the world and wait until terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Creative-mode world and can fly and execute commands.

steps.action: Press Esc and navigate to Options -> Video Settings -> Particles. Cycle the Particles option until it reads All, then select Done until gameplay resumes.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with the Particles setting on All.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to move to the construction coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The player is near X=0, Y=66, Z=0 and the surrounding chunks have finished rendering.

steps.action: Open chat, execute the following command including the leading slash, and wait for command feedback. This clears the volume that will contain the reconstructed test arena.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the fill command completed, and the test volume around the player is unobstructed.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to create a three-block-wide, seventeen-block-long stone runway. Its top walking surface will be at Y=65.
steps.success_cue: A stone runway extends from Z=-8 through Z=8, spanning X=-1 through X=1 at Y=64.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to place a red concrete strip immediately beside the negative-X side of the runway.
steps.success_cue: A red concrete strip runs parallel to the runway at X=-2 and Y=64.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to place a blue concrete strip immediately beside the positive-X side of the runway.
steps.success_cue: A blue concrete strip runs parallel to the runway at X=2 and Y=64.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to create an invisible barrier wall directly above the red concrete strip. The wall is intended to stop the golem from entering the red strip's horizontal space or standing on it.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that 51 barrier blocks were placed along the negative-X side of the runway.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to create an invisible barrier wall directly above the blue concrete strip. The wall is intended to stop the golem from entering the blue strip's horizontal space or standing on it.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that 51 barrier blocks were placed along the positive-X side of the runway.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to close the Z=-9 end of the arena with an invisible barrier wall.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that 15 barrier blocks were placed across the Z=-9 end.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to close the Z=9 end of the arena with an invisible barrier wall.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that 15 barrier blocks were placed across the Z=9 end; the runway is now enclosed by invisible walls while the red and blue concrete remain outside the walkable interior.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the following command to create one iron golem at the center of the stone runway. Do not add NoAI or other entity data, because the golem must be able to walk naturally.
steps.success_cue: One iron golem is standing upright near the center of the enclosed runway and is not embedded in a wall or block.

steps.action: Open chat and switch the player to Spectator mode so the player can take a clear viewing position without physically obstructing the golem.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Spectator mode and can fly through blocks.

steps.action: Open chat and teleport to an elevated viewing position near one end of the arena, then aim the camera at the golem's feet and the edges of the stone runway. Do not left-click the golem, because that would enter its spectator view.
steps.success_cue: The complete runway and the area immediately around the iron golem's feet are visible, with the camera outside the enclosed walking space.

steps.action: Do not interact with the golem. Wait for its normal wandering AI to move it horizontally along the runway. Continue only when its position changes and its legs perform at least one clear walking stride; if it merely turns its head or rotates in place, keep waiting. Once walking begins, immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without repeatedly spawning more golems or forcing excessive movement.
steps.success_cue: The iron golem has begun a clear horizontal walking stride while remaining inside the barrier-bounded runway, and its feet and the nearby red, blue, and stone blocks are in view.

stor.handoff_condition: The iron golem has just begun walking horizontally inside the reconstructed runway, cannot enter the red or blue side strips because of the barrier walls above them, particle rendering remains set to All, and the camera is aimed at the golem's feet. Begin particle observation now.
uncertainties: The report's exact setup is conveyed through an unavailable image attachment after the text "Build a setup like this:". The supplied text does not preserve the blocks, dimensions, orientation, or spatial arrangement shown in that image.

The sentence "Create an iron golem within" is truncated in the supplied report, apparently because another attachment or inline element is missing. It is assumed to mean creating the golem within the pictured setup.

The command-built stone runway with red and blue side strips under barrier walls is a practical reconstruction, not a claim that these were the blocks or geometry shown by the reporter. It provides visually distinct nearby blocks that the golem is prevented from occupying or colliding with.

No game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, or entity-creation method is specified. Creative mode, a disposable Superflat world, coordinates near the origin, and the summon command are execution choices made to minimize unrelated setup.

Natural iron-golem wandering has nondeterministic timing. The report only says to observe as it walks and does not provide a method for inducing movement. The plan therefore waits for an unforced walking stride rather than adding a hostile target, lead, or movement command that could change the test conditions.
Web verification using permitted Mojang/Minecraft domains confirmed the historical pre-release context but did not expose the five attachment images or restore the truncated reproduction text.

source_meta._title: Barrier particles aren't shown if particles are set to minimal

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 14w06b, using an unmodified client in a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled so the unobtainable Barrier item can be acquired with a version-compatible command.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 14w06b, preferably from a separate launcher installation/profile so its historical settings and world files are isolated from newer versions.
Use the normal Minecraft resource pack and no client mods, shaders, or optimization modifications that alter particle rendering.
A keyboard and mouse are available. The instructions name the default controls; use the equivalent bound control if keys have been reassigned.
No particular seed, biome, structure, coordinates, difficulty, or world type are specified by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for snapshot 14w06b and start the game. Do not substitute the listed fix version 23w40a.
steps.success_cue: The 14w06b title screen is displayed and the version text identifies the running snapshot as 14w06b.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and create the world. Using a new world is a deterministic way to establish the Creative-mode condition; the report does not require a specific existing world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a world in Creative mode and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Wait without opening menus until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Solid ground is visible nearby, chunks are no longer visibly appearing around the player, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the pause menu with the default pause control.
steps.success_cue: The Game menu is open.

steps.action: Open the general options screen.
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is displayed.

steps.action: Open the video settings screen.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen is displayed and contains the Particles setting.

steps.action: Click the Particles button repeatedly until its displayed value is Minimal. Stop as soon as it reads Minimal; do not leave it on All or Decreased.
steps.success_cue: The button on the Video Settings screen visibly reads "Particles: Minimal".

steps.action: Use Done to leave Video Settings, use Done again to leave Options, and select Back to Game if the pause menu remains open.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with the Particles option still set to Minimal.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input using the default chat control. The next command must be executed in in-game chat, not in a server console.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Type the exact 14w06b-compatible give command, including its leading slash, and press Enter. This supplies one Barrier because the Barrier is not normally selected from the historical Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and a Barrier item appears in the player's inventory, normally in the first available hotbar slot.

steps.action: If the Barrier did not enter the hotbar automatically, press E to open the inventory, locate the Barrier item, and move it into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots displayed along the bottom of the gameplay screen. Close the inventory with E after moving the item.
steps.success_cue: A Barrier item is present in one of the nine hotbar slots and normal gameplay view is restored.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Barrier by pressing that slot's number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling until the slot is highlighted. Keep this item selected for the rest of the reproduction; barrier visibility in this snapshot is activated while a Creative-mode player holds a Barrier.
steps.success_cue: The Barrier slot has the hotbar selection highlight and the Barrier item is the player's actively held item.

steps.action: Move to an exposed solid ground block with an empty air block directly above it. Remain close enough to place a block on its top face without changing the active hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing within placement reach of a visible solid ground block, and the air immediately above that block is unobstructed.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top face of the chosen solid ground block. Keep the Barrier selected and do not aim at grass, a flower, an entity, or another interactable object that could consume the click.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the top face of the chosen ground block and the Barrier remains selected.

steps.action: Right-click once to place one Barrier in the air block immediately above the targeted ground block. After clicking, do not scroll the mouse wheel, press another hotbar number, open the inventory, or move far away; continue actively holding the Barrier.
steps.success_cue: The placement action has just been performed at the targeted block space, the Barrier remains selected in the active hotbar slot, and the player remains directly beside the placement location.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just manually placed a Barrier on top of the selected ground block in Creative mode, the Video Settings particle level remains Minimal, the Barrier item remains selected in the active hotbar slot, and the player remains beside and facing the placement location. Begin particle-rendering observation now without changing the held item or graphics settings.
uncertainties: The report provides no seed, coordinates, world type, or required terrain, so the plan uses an arbitrary newly generated world and the first convenient exposed solid ground block.

The report does not specify how to obtain the Barrier item. The plan uses the version-compatible command `/give @p minecraft:barrier 1` because Barrier is not normally obtained from the historical Creative inventory.

The report says to switch into Creative mode but does not indicate that a transition from another game mode is itself required. The plan creates the test world directly in Creative mode to minimize unrelated actions.

Barrier placement produces an invisible solid block, and the success cue deliberately does not use the presence or absence of its red particle icon because evaluating that rendering is the responsibility of the observation subsystem.
